N7_CAPACITY_INSTRUMENT_CALIBRATION.json.task: N7 — calibration of the capacity instrument (G7 daily sim)
N7_CAPACITY_INSTRUMENT_CALIBRATION.json.why: G7 is about to be asked whether the book has a capacity limit below AVUV's floor. It has never been asked whether it can tell a capacity effect from nothing.

Z_known_zero.reading: bias is the CAGR the simulator invents in a world with no frictions and no capacity limit. It is the floor below which no capacity claim from this instrument means anything.

C_known_cost.reading: cost per dollar traded is analytic here: half-spread plus slippage plus commission. The instrument either recovers it or it is mis-charging every book it has ever priced.

K_known_cap.reading: liquidity tightens down the list. Degradation must be zero where the cap cannot bind and must grow as it does. A non-monotone column means the instrument is reading something other than capacity.

I_impact_term.reading: cost per dollar traded is IDENTICAL across a million-fold range of liquidity. G7 charges half-spread + slippage + commission on notional and nothing that grows with participation, so it prices capacity as DELAY (orders that cannot fill are carried) and never as PRICE (moving the market against yourself). That is the dominant capacity cost in the literature and this instrument cannot see it.

verdict.statement: PARTIALLY CALIBRATED. What it does well: false positives 0% in a world with no capacity effect (max invented CAGR 0.03%/yr), cost per dollar traded recovered to 0.00 bps, degradation monotone in liquidity tightness. What it CANNOT do: price impact. Cost per dollar traded is identical across a 1,000,000x range of liquidity (range 0.00 bps), so G7 models capacity as DELAY and never as PRICE. Even with a name's whole daily volume equal to the position, degradation reached only 0.065%/yr — because an annual clock has a year to work orders down. CONSEQUENCE: a capacity number from this instrument is a LOWER BOUND, and CAPACITY-EDGE-1 may not report a capacity limit from it without either adding a participation-dependent impact term or labelling the result as delay-only.

T1c_ENSEMBLE_COST_NORMALIZED.json.task: T1c — the ensemble cost claim, normalised for the NAV path
T1c_ENSEMBLE_COST_NORMALIZED.json.corrects: NIGHT-7B's 'the ensemble is CHEAPER' ($313,775 vs $333,165). Both arms start at the same NAV and end at different ones, so total cost DOLLARS reward the arm that compounded less. The panel says the turnover RATES are equal (0.468 vs 0.468), which is the tell.
T1c_ENSEMBLE_COST_NORMALIZED.json.capital_treatment: each NAV rung is INDEPENDENTLY re-simulated — costs are never scaled from another rung, because participation caps and impact are nonlinear in size

claim_check_calibration.reading: false_positive_rate is the share of INVENTED numbers this checker would have called informatively backed. Read every coverage figure against it.

docs/NIGHT8_VERDICT_2026-08-10.md.reading: Three states, not two. INFORMATIVELY BACKED: a receipt holds this number and a perturbed version of it would NOT have matched, so the match carries information. MATCHED BUT UNINFORMATIVE: a receipt holds it, but so many scalars sit nearby that any number of this shape would have matched — small integers and round figures live here and the check has no power over them. UNBACKED: no receipt in the programme holds it. None of the three says anything about the QUALIFIER attached to the number in prose, which is this programme's actual citation failure mode.
